source_note: Hand-curated from the Oracle delivery study (SEC 10-Q/10-K/8-K, earnings calls, oracle.com, state permits, utility filings, county documents) and its 2026-11-19 audit, which checked every checkpoint against primary sources and dropped those that did not hold. 'Checkpoint' marks a date by which something should be confirmed; it is not a forecast.
rules: Oracle's own results (about two weeks after each quarter end) are the only source of MW delivered and of site-by-site confirmation. 'Delivered' is not formally defined and looks like IT load; quarterly MW is lumpy, so judge two-quarter averages, not one quarter.
At site level, power decides the date: air permits, gas supply and transmission approvals are the most useful early warnings.

oracle.com wording is a weak signal: the US page dropped every date in a 2026-11-12 revision (65 locale copies still show them), which may be legal clean-up. It counts only if the December call does not restate the timelines.

Confirmation only: a new Oracle IP block or region certificate confirms a campus is live (public regions: median 2 months ahead, n=11; dedicated OpenAI capacity: one case). Its absence is not evidence of delay.
Background only: Texas building-registration dates are owner estimates and inspection status may lag completion by up to a year; job-posting lead times rest on one site (Abilene).

sites.name: Shackelford (Frontier)
sites.status: Later than Vantage's original 2H 2026; first-phase power already permitted
sites.note: First buildings run on standard air permit 180842 (issued 2025-07-17; ~700 MW per a secondary source). Full-campus permit 182467 gates later buildings, not first delivery. Texas registrations TX301–TX310 are whole-building records (shell plus fit-out), unlike Abilene's split records, so no delivery date is inferred from them; TX311 is an office. Owner-estimated completions of the first three (2027-02-15, 04-19, 05-18) are consistent with 1H27 and were unchanged in archives of 10/1 and 11/7. Vantage's 'delivery' (shell and power to Oracle) and Oracle's 'customer delivery' may be different milestones.

sites.name: Doña Ana (Project Jupiter)
sites.status: Highest risk: air permit and gas lateral both unapproved
sites.note: The only planned primary power is an on-site Bloom fuel-cell microgrid, which needs the NMED air permit and gas from the Green Chile lateral. The county MOU's 'initial capacity Q4 2026' and 'phase 1 Q3 2028' are expectations, not lease covenants (the lease's completion date is 2055-10-01). The 7/31 county report's '~9%' has no stated basis and covers all four buildings. County breach notices: 10/27 (5–0) potential breach over the power plan, 30-day cure; 11/10 (4–0) missed jobs reports (paperwork). The worst remedy is lease termination and loss of the tax break, not a construction stop.

gap: Oracle discloses no cumulative or contracted MW, and its 'leases not yet commenced' ($288bn) are not split by site. Doña Ana, Wisconsin and federal (FERC) dockets block automated access, so those checks are manual. The ~10 GW by end-FY28 target appears only in secondary summaries with unclear units (IT vs gross power), so it is not used as a threshold.
